title: Install an Electrical Receptacle in a Kitchen Island: Box Location, Wiring, and AFCI/GFCI Testing

summary: This Old House chronicles a kitchen-island upgrade to add a dedicated receptacle where none existed. Heath and Katie locate a feed that presumably serves the island, verify that power can be safely de-energized (using a non-contact tester and a meter), and then trace the wire with a toner to confirm its path toward a wall outlet location. They mark and cut a precise opening in the island’s cabinet/back panel, then install a new junction box and route BX/metal-clad cable through a protected bushing with a 90° connector. After wiring the receptacle (ground to green, neutral to silver, hot to brass) and securing the box, they install an AFCI-protected circuit (and test a GFCI function) to ensure protection for the new outlet. The finished test confirms the mixer and other devices work, and the homeowners can use the island for baking with confidence. Throughout, the video emphasizes safety steps (de-energize, confirm with a meter, proper notch and spacing, and appropriate connections) and documentation of the process from locating the feed to testing the finished circuit.
